# With the cgo option, gtk4 connects a handler through GLib's
# g_signal_connect_data, the handler crossing as a C callback: the test's
# clicks are GTK's "clicked", which reaches the closure through the
# dispatcher sngl_callbacks.go exports, and a switch's notify::active is
# connected through the GParamSpec-taking shape of its own.

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"
import go "sngl:language/go"
import test "sngl:test"

output {
    go {
        gtk4(gir="builtin", cgo=true)
    }
}

component main ui.node {
    var n = 0
    var on = false
    ui.vbox {
        ui.button #count(text="{n}", @click {
            n += 1
        })
        ui.toggle(:checked=on, label="on")
    }
}

ui.window(title="t") {
    main()
}

func testClickReachesTheClosure(t test.Test, c main) {
    c.count.click()
    c.count.click()
    t.assert(c.n == 2)
}
-- testrun/gtk4/go/app.sngl/main/1 --

  "results": [
    {
      "Desc": "ClickReachesTheClosure",
      "Passed": true
    }
  ]
}
